findings.summary: 3D Slash is a voxel-based 3D modeling application designed to simplify 3D design for beginners and educators. It represents geometry using an octree of cuboids, enabling implicit level-of-detail control. The software provides a stone-cutter metaphor toolset for adding, removing, and coloring cuboids, and outputs .STL files for 3D printing. It is available across web browsers, Windows, macOS, Linux, and Raspberry Pi, and integrates with platforms like Thingiverse, Google Drive, and Onshape. The software is proprietary and uses a custom functional language called Metal. Content created online is licensed under Creative Commons BY-NC-SA unless a premium subscription is purchased.

mechanisms.title: Octree-based geometry representation
mechanisms.explanation: Geometry is represented as a tree of deformed cuboid shapes. Each cuboid can be full, empty, or subdivided into eight smaller cuboids. This structure implicitly defines level of detail by cutting the tree at arbitrary depth, allowing the software to manage model complexity without explicit user settings.

mechanisms.title: Stone-cutter metaphor toolset
mechanisms.explanation: The user interface provides tools modeled after stone-cutting actions: a hammer to remove cuboids, a trowel to add them, a chisel to remove slices, a brush to set colors, and wood filler to add slices. These tools map intuitive editing actions to cuboid manipulation within the octree structure.
